notes:
Summary: Closed-lost. Ironbark selected Together for an on-prem POC and eventual rollout. Main drivers: mandatory on-prem deployment + HSM integration, stronger ROI for their large token volumes after Together's quantized model offering, and an internal ML infra lead who pushed for Together after a short vendor consolidation exercise.

Timeline / activity (shorthand):
- 2025-11-02: Initial intro call (Maya + Daniel) — discovered high-frequency risk-scoring workload, 200 req/s target, sub-100ms tail latency goal.
- 2025-11-12: Sent pricing deck and architecture notes (see drive link). POC proposal drafted.
- 2025-12-01: Security questionnaire submitted by Ironbark; SOC2 and KMS flagged as mandatory.
- 2025-12-15: Demo w/ latency targets — Redwood demo went well, initial perf numbers promising on hosted.
- 2026-01-05: POC kickoff discussions; Ironbark narrowed to 3 vendors (Together, Fireworks, Redwood).
- 2026-01-20: Security review escalated (SEC-874). Customer asked for HSM/KMS design and audit log retention policy.
- 2026-01-28: Short POC executed with small dataset; Together offered on-prem test image and HSM integration faster than Redwood could commit.
- 2026-02-10: Final procurement meeting — procurement/IT favored Together for perceived faster delivery and better on-prem pricing. AE notified.

Key requirements (from calls):
- "We need an on-prem stack with HSM and audit logs, data never leaves the VPC." — Head of IT.
- Latency SLOs: 50-120ms p95 for scoring calls.
- Throughput: sustained 150-250 requests/sec for peak windows.
- Cost sensitivity: high — long-tail token costs will scale quickly.
- Model preferences: open LLaMA-derivative family or optimized llama-variants; willingness to accept quantized weights if quality preserved.

Why we lost (notes / analysis):
- Together shipped an on-prem test image + HSM integration faster and provided a clearer contract for data residency.
- Pricing: Together's committed reserved nodes for the POC undercut Redwood on the projected ARR model. Ironbark prioritized predictable monthly spend.
- Internal champion change: their ML infra lead (advocated for Redwood early) left the company mid-eval; new lead had existing relationships with Together engineers.
- Security comfort: Ironbark's security team felt Together's doc examples for audit logs and KMS were more mature.

Engagement notes / next steps for Redwood:
- Mark as closed-lost in CRM, capture lessons: accelerate on-prem HSM reference playbook and tighten POC timelines for enterprise buyers.
- Suggested follow-up cadence: check-in 3 months post-rollout (approx. 2026-05 to 2026-07) to see operational pain points.
- Possible re-entry angles: stronger TCO comparison for quantized models; offer migration plan and hybrid fallback (dedicated + private) that minimizes downtime during cutover.

Artifacts: pricing deck (drive link), security questionnaire (attached SEC-874), Fireflies transcript ff_20251112_q3v9b8 (call w/Head of IT).

Short CRM-style notes from last call: "Procurement picked Together — faster on-prem + price. We'll revisit in 3-6 months if issues. Thanks for the quick turnaround — keep us in the loop."

Blocked items (left unresolved): final HSM design doc (we provided draft), formal SLA for on-prem availability, legal's template for data residency.

Owner notes: good technical fit, lost due to project timing + security comfort with competitor; recommend adding a short win-back plan to enterprise playbook.
